principles.text: Overnight gap risk after entry cannot be managed away; it is part of the game.
Small caps carry higher gap risk and lower liquidity, so he sizes them 10-20% smaller than normal as a risk premium.
Gap-downs into converging anchored VWAPs (e.g. 4-week) are tradeable shorts; plain gap-down breakdowns away from those levels (e.g. DELL) he does not trade.
For shorts, focus on weak names below their EMAs; don't short strong names that are still above key EMAs.
Short bias is set by the big-picture market structure and breadth; breadth is a pretty important indicator to him.
After a short stops out, if the index gaps above all EMAs and holds, the reason to short no longer exists - stop re-attempting the short side.

If a short stops out but the stock has not broken any resistance or shown strength (still below declining 21, prior breakdown high), a re-entry (e.g. hourly candle breakdown) is still valid; a QQQ close above the declining 21 is the first warning sign to stop shorting or flip long.
Covers shorts at weekly EMAs used as support (e.g. Russell 50-week EMA); treats shorts as shorter swings and covers into weakness rather than trying to capture the whole move.
When traveling/off the desk he reduces focus and covers shorts rather than managing them; there will be more entries if the market really turns weak.
Never try to be right or nail the entry and exit; don't treat every trade (especially shorts) as a home run - multi-month trends offer plenty of entries.
After a good run, slow down: overtrading with a cushion is behavioral slippage that hurts the next A-grade trade (death by 1,000 cuts).
Uses hard stop orders placed after entry, so exits involve no hesitation or personal judgment; ignoring stops early on turned 3% losses into 5-8% outliers.
Big winners never hit or even come close to the stop after entry; a stock going below the stop is a bad sign, so exit without second thoughts.
Holding period for shorts depends on how fast the stock drops, not a fixed number of days.
Best timing for pullback shorts is when the general market/index is at its own EMAs; shorting individual names at their EMAs while the market is extended has a lower success rate.
Before shorting crypto he wants the index and Bitcoin both at resistance together, not with the stock market extended from its declining EMAs.
No limit on the number of stop-outs per stock or per day.
